body_text: Reaffirms Second Quarter and Full-Year Fiscal 2026 Guidance July 1, 2026 – PITTSBURGH – (BUSINESS WIRE) – American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. (NYSE: AEO) today announced that after 25 years of service, Mike Mathias, Executive Vice President – Chief Financial Officer will transition to serve as a full-time non-executive strategic advisor to Jay Schottenstein, Executive Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, effective August 3, 2026. Ravi Thanawala will succeed Mathias as Executive Vice President – Chief Financial Officer, also effective August 3, 2026. To ensure a seamless leadership transition, Mathias will collaborate closely with Thanawala through the remainder of AEO’s 2026 fiscal year and continue supporting Schottenstein through July 30, 2027. “I want to extend my immense appreciation to Mike for his exceptional leadership and dedicated service. Mike’s history with AEO runs incredibly deep. He began his career with the company in 1998, and though his professional journey took him elsewhere for a time, his love for AEO’s brands and people ultimately brought him back in 2017, where his significant impact led to his promotion to CFO in 2020. Throughout his tenure, he has successfully guided our organization through a rapidly evolving retail landscape and a period of significant growth, which is why I’ve asked Mike to step into the role of strategic advisor to me. Mike’s financial expertise and strategic foresight have been instrumental in strengthening the foundation of our business, driving long-term value and positioning AEO for a bright future,” said Jay Schottenstein . Schottenstein continued, “We are pleased to welcome Ravi Thanawala to the executive team. His extensive retail background, dynamic leadership style and proven track record of delivering operational excellence for consumer-facing brands will position us well for long-term success.” “I am incredibly proud of the financial and operational milestones we have achieved during my time as CFO,” said Mike Mathias. “I want to thank Jay, the Board of Directors and my colleagues for their partnership and extend my appreciation to our exceptional finance team for their dedication and resilience. I leave the finance function in highly capable hands, backed by the deep bench strength of our talented leaders–and I have full confidence in AEO’s continued momentum in the marketplace as I support a smooth transition.” Incoming Executive Vice President – Chief Financial Officer, Ravi Thanawala said, “American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. has been a premier specialty retailer for generations with longstanding market leadership, and I am honored to step into the role as CFO. I have long admired AEO’s powerful portfolio of beloved lifestyle brands, including American Eagle and Aerie, as well as the disciplined financial foundation and strong operational framework that Jay, Mike and the team have established. My immediate priority is working with Mike to ensure a seamless transition that maintains organizational momentum. Looking ahead, I am excited to partner with Jay and leadership to accelerate long-term strategic initiatives, maintain financial discipline and unlock new avenues for profitable growth that will help to maximize value for our shareholders.” In addition, AEO today reaffirmed its second quarter and full-year 2026 financial guidance, as previously announced in its earnings release on May 28, 2026. * * * * About Ravi Thanawala Ravi Thanawala was appointed the Chief Financial Officer and President, North America of Papa John’s International, Inc. in November 2025 after serving as Chief Financial Officer and EVP, International since September 2024. Thanawala also served as Papa John’s Interim Chief Executive Officer from March 2024 to August 2024, after joining the company as Chief Financial Officer in July 2023. He previously held the role of Chief Financial Officer of Nike North America at Nike, Inc. from June 2020 to July 2023. From 2018 to 2020, Thanawala also served as the Global VP and CFO of the Converse brand. In addition, he was the Global VP of Retail Excellence from 2016 to 2018. Prior to Nike, Inc., Thanawala spent eight years at ANN INC. with progressively increasing responsibilities in finance and operations. He served in the finance leadership role for LOFT; led ANN INC’s Asia operations, global logistics and international trade based in Hong Kong; and rose to the position of CFO of the ANN INC. business, a subsidiary of Ascena Retail Group, Inc. About American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. (NYSE: AEO) is a leading global specialty retailer with a portfolio of beloved apparel brands including American Eagle, Aerie, OFFL/NE by Aerie, Todd Snyder and Unsubscribed. Rooted in optimism, inclusivity and authenticity, AEO’s brands empower every customer to celebrate their unique personal style by offering casual, comfortable, timeless outfitting and high-quality products that are made to last. AEO Inc. operates stores in the United States, Canada and Mexico, with merchandise available in more than 30 countries through a global network of license partners. Additionally, the company operates a robust e-commerce business across its brands. For more information, visit aeo-inc.com . title: The Superior Mechanical Resistance of Nexa® Vials for Improved Efficiency and Safety
summary: Breakage reduction starts with container strength. This article looks at mechanical resistance in pharma vials, with a focus on Stevanato Group’s Nexa®.
body_text: JAN 8 | 2025 The Superior Mechanical Resistance of Nexa® Vials for Improved Efficiency and Safety Executive Summary Introduction: Ensuring the mechanical resistance of pharmaceutical glass vials is crucial for safe and efficient drug delivery. While allowing for high throughput and efficiency, the bulk Fill & Finish process exerts high level of stress on glass containers, such as glass-to-glass contact and vertical loads, which can lead to cosmetic defects and breakages. Superior vial quality mitigates the negative impact of this stress, improving filling process performance and output as well as reducing the risk of container breakage during transport. 2R vials This study aims to experimentally demonstrate the improved mechanical resistance performance of Nexa®. By comparing the 2R ISO format vial in Nexa® and Fina® platforms, this study highlights how Nexa® vials provide superior mechanical resistance, which translates into several operational benefits. Test Methodology Mechanical resistance was assessed using two quantitative techniques 1. Vertical Compression Test (VC): This test measures the maximum force a vial can withstand before failure when subjected to axial stress. vertical compression_2R_pre and post Figure 1: Sample before (left) and after (right) VC test. 2. Burst Test (BT): This test is performed to apply internal pressure to the glass container to obtain its maximum value of internal pressure resistance. burst test_2R_pre and post Figure 2: Sample before (left) and after (right) the burst test. Both tests compared Nexa® and Fina® vials. From the results achieved (VC and BT), Nexa® vials showed consistent superior mechanical resistance . Key Results 2R ISO vials In the Vertical Compression Test , Nexa® vials demonstrated an average maximum force of at least 3x Fina®. vertical compression_2R Figure 3: Boxplot of Vertical Compression results for 2R Fina® and Nexa® vials. title: How to Win Q4 2026: 4 Trends Shaping the Season
summary: For advertisers, no quarter carries more weight than Q4, and 2026 is shaping up to be another strong one. EMARKETER predicts holiday spending will increase year-over-year (YoY), for retail as a whole and even more so for ecommerce. Q4 has always been competitive, but the holiday shopping landscape continues to shift in ways that make […]
body_text: For advertisers, no quarter carries more weight than Q4, and 2026 is shaping up to be another strong one. EMARKETER predicts holiday spending will increase year-over-year (YoY), for retail as a whole and even more so for ecommerce. Q4 has always been competitive, but the holiday shopping landscape continues to shift in ways that make standing out harder than ever. Here’s what market research and MNTN advertiser data reveal about the trends shaping Q4 2026, and what they mean for your strategy. Streaming Owns the Largest Share of TV Viewership and Q4 Is When It Matters Most Streaming has cemented itself as the dominant way Americans watch television. As of April 2026 , it commanded 47.6% of U.S. household TV viewing (more than broadcast and cable combined). That split holds in Q4 too, and it may matter more during the holiday season than any other time of year. In December 2025 , streaming captured 47.5% of all TV viewing, while broadcast fell to 21.4% and cable dropped to 20.2%. And within the Q4 window, specific dates carry outsized weight. In 2025, streaming viewership was up 11% during Thanksgiving week and 19% during Christmas week, compared with average non-holiday weeks. As Q4 streaming viewership hits new highs, MNTN advertiser performance data points in the same direction. Among MNTN advertisers who ran campaigns in both Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, key metrics improved YoY, some by significant margins: +448% Average Conversion Rate +121% Average Average Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) +80% Average Visit Rate -10% Average Average Cost per Acquisition (CPA) Mobile shopping’s rise isn’t just about convenience: ever-growing second-screen usage is fueling it too. Nearly two-thirds of U.S. social network users are projected to be actively using a second screen while watching TV or streaming in 2026, a figure expected to reach 81.9% of the total U.S. population by 2027. And the shopping behavior that follows is measurable: 34% of U.S. TV viewers have purchased merchandise inspired by a show, and 31% have shopped for products tied to what they’re watching via QR codes or in-show links. Second-screen usage is surging across all age groups, and this is particularly notable in Q4. In November 2025, 63% of consumers ages 18-24 and 61% of those ages 25-34 viewed videos on their phones while watching TV (up 2% and 1% since 2022, respectively). But the most notable growth came from older generations: 52% of consumers ages 45-54 and 35% ages 55-64 also use a second screen while streaming, an increase of 13% and 15% since 2022. Travel Tuesday is Now One of Q4’s Most Valuable Moments for Travel Brands Q4 marks the unofficial start of Wave Season , the travel industry’s peak booking period, when consumers are actively planning trips months in advance. BFCM has long been a strong window for travel brands, but in recent years a new moment has emerged in its wake: Travel Tuesday (the day after Cyber Monday). Travel Tuesday now generates 3.5x more bookings than the average day, with searches for the event up more than 5x over a two-year period. Together, Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Travel Tuesday have become what travel marketing agency Sojern refers to as a “perfect storm”: a concentrated window of urgency and deal volume covering flights, hotels, and packages. A “value-first traveler” mindset is reshaping how consumers engage with this shopping period. They’re still spending on travel, but choosing with precision, seeking packages, points, and experiences over premium-priced impulse bookings. MNTN advertiser data supports the importance of Q4 and Travel Tuesday in particular. Among travel brands active in both Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, the following key metrics improved YoY: +133% Average Visit Rate +56% Average ROAS +49% Average Conversion Rate On top of this, average CPA and CPV fell sharply. Within Q4, the week of Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday was the strongest of the quarter across revenue, ROAS, and CPA. Travel Tuesday itself was the standout day of the entire BFCM window, driving the highest revenue, the lowest CPA, and an average order value (AOV) that was 147% higher than Black Friday. The implications of these findings extend beyond travel brands. Elevated purchase intent that builds through BFCM doesn’t switch off after Cyber Monday. Instead, it carries into the days that follow, and beyond. For advertisers in industries that can have longer purchase cycles (e.g. financial services, automotive, education, health, technology) the BFCM window is an opportunity to reach consumers who are already primed. Just as travel brands use Travel Tuesday to lock in bookings for trips months away, brands in other industries can use Q4 to plant intent that converts well into the new year. Video Game Spending Is Approaching All-Time Highs, and Q4 Is Make-or-Break U.S. consumer spending on video games reached $60.7 billion in 2025 (the second-highest on record) and 2026 has the potential to reach a new all-time high. Q4 is a key piece to this, as 45% of single-player games drop between mid-August and mid-November. This year, that includes the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19th, which is expected to drive a significant spike in sales. The biggest structural shift in gaming right now is where spending happens. Physical game sales hit a 30-year low of $1.5 billion in 2025, even as total spending grew, driven by digital downloads, cloud gaming, and subscriptions. Subscription spending increased by 20% in 2025 , making it the single largest growth driver in the industry. This shift has real implications for how gaming audiences are reached: as consumers move away from physical retail and toward digital-based access (which will only accelerate in light of Sony’s decision to end physical disc production by early 2028) TV video content has become one of the most effective ways to connect with them. Gaming audiences aren’t just playing, they’re watching movies, sports, and shows like everyone else, making Q4’s record streaming environment a prime opportunity for gaming advertisers. For non-gaming brands, the subscription trend is a signal worth watching. Consumers are increasingly comfortable giving and receiving digital products as opposed to physical ones. For brands outside of gaming, Q4 is a prime window to position subscription offerings as gifts or purposeful new-year investments. ‘Tis the Season to Get Your Q4 Strategy Set Q4 2026 is set up to be one of the most opportunity-rich on record. Streaming reach is at an all-time high, and mobile has permanently shifted how consumers shop during the holidays. Meanwhile, moments like Travel Tuesday and major gaming releases are concentrating purchase intent in specific windows that produce powerful performance. Brands that understand where that intent lives (and show up there consistently) will be the ones that make the most of it. For advertisers looking to reach engaged, high-intent holiday audiences across all of these moments, Connected TV (CTV) is uniquely positioned to deliver.

title: AI Is Exposing Fragmented Systems in Financial Services
summary: AI exposes fragmented systems in financial services. Integrated data, simplified operations, and real-time intelligence are critical.
body_text: The biggest problem in financial services is not AI readiness, it’s structural complexity. Video: How SAP and SAP Fioneer Are Shaping the Future Watch now That was the takeaway from a recent conversation between SAP CFO Dominik Asam and SAP Fioneer CEO Matthias Tomann. Their conversation touched on topics like the future of financial services , the role of AI, and the growing importance of integrated enterprise platforms. For decades, banks and insurers have built operating models around regulatory fragmentation, country-specific requirements, layered systems, and continuous workaround solutions. As a result, the industry is running on patchwork architecture that is expensive to maintain, slow to change, and fundamentally misaligned with how AI works. Partnership built for financial services innovation Since joining forces in 2021, SAP and SAP Fioneer have significantly expanded their joint capabilities for the financial services sector. As Tomann highlighted in the conversation, the partnership has already delivered substantial momentum for SAP Fioneer: R&D investment increased by 120% Annual software sales more than doubled Major customers successfully transitioned to SAP Cloud ERP The platform evolved into a richer, more scalable, and highly capable ecosystem Together, the companies are combining SAP’s trusted cloud and data infrastructure with SAP Fioneer’s deep financial services expertise to help institutions simplify operations, modernize core systems, and prepare for the AI-driven future. Executives from both companies will be exploring these critical topics further at their annual SAP & SAP Fioneer Financial Services Forum 2026, which is now open for registration. AI is not the starting point, data integration is Everyone wants AI, but AI can only create value from integrated data, real-time access, and standardized processes. But most financial institutions still operate on the opposite: fragmented foundations. That reality will define the winners over the next five years. The organizations that succeed will not be the ones experimenting with the most models. They will be the ones that establish unified, trusted, real-time enterprise data with strong governance. That is the real competitive advantage. But even that is only part of the story. The next phase is not just about using AI to analyze better; it is about AI executing work. We are now seeing a fundamental shift: from systems that store and report information to systems that act on that information in real time, orchestrating end-to-end processes across the business. This marks the transition to the Autonomous Enterprise , SAP’s vision for the future of business where AI does not just support decisions but increasingly drives execution, within clearly defined guardrails. Financial services can no longer afford “patchwork architecture” This shift makes one thing clear: The traditional approach to building IT landscapes is no longer viable. For years, many financial institutions solved problems incrementally—another point solution, another integration layer, another workaround. But eventually every workaround becomes technical debt and integration is the single largest IT cost category. Tomann made clear during the conversation that the emphasis must be on simplification rather than adding more complexity. What SAP and SAP Fioneer are driving is not another modernization cycle. It is a structural shift toward comprehensive, integrated platforms and AI driven processes that replace fragmentation, not sit on top of it. The result is a scalable financial services platform where core banking, lending, reporting, insurance, and analytics operate within an integrated architecture instead of disconnected silos. Real-time finance is becoming a strategic requirement Real-time capability is becoming foundational to competitiveness—whether it’s risk management, regulatory reporting, customer experience, fraud prevention, treasury operations, or AI-driven decision making. Institutions that can act on integrated data instantly will have a major advantage over those still moving information between disconnected systems overnight. With integrated data and AI embedded in core processes, finance is moving toward continuous financial intelligence: Forecasting becomes dynamic and always up to date Risk is detected and assessed in real time Closing processes become increasingly automated Decisions are guided by AI based on live business context Increasingly, AI assistants and agents take over execution of finance processes, from planning and risk management to invoicing and financial close, under strict governance. The role of finance shifts from reporting on the business to steering the business in real time. AI will reward those who simplify One of the most striking statements from Asam during the discussion is that SAP is already seeing 10x performance improvements from AI-driven process improvements. But it also highlights something many organizations still underestimate: just how much AI rewards those who standardize. The more fragmented the processes and data structures are, the harder it becomes to operationalize AI at scale. In contrast, organizations with standardized platforms, harmonized data, and integrated workflows will accelerate much faster. That is why modernization conversations today are no longer simply “IT projects.” They are business strategy discussions. Future of financial services will be built on trust, scale, and intelligence Financial services organizations are operating in an increasingly complex geopolitical and regulatory environment. Infrastructure decisions are no longer just about performance and cost, they are about compliance, security, operational resilience, and national requirements. This is why scalable, enterprise-grade cloud platforms are becoming so critical. The institutions that thrive in the next era of financial services will be the ones that can combine trusted data, integrated operations, AI-enabled processes, scalable infrastructure, and regulatory resilience into a single operating model. The future of financial services will not be defined by isolated AI experiments. It will be defined by who can build the most intelligent, connected, and adaptable enterprise foundation for what comes next. Learn more about SAP solutions for financial services here . title: Palladyne AI Announces Preliminary Second Quarter 2026 Revenue of Approximately $5.8 Million and Backlog of Approximately $24.0 Million
summary: Preliminary Q2 2026 results: Palladyne AI revenue rose to approximately $5.8 million, up ~480% year over year, with backlog reaching $24.0 million.
body_text: Preliminary second quarter revenue expected to be approximately $5.8 million, up approximately 480% year over year and 66% sequentially Backlog grew to approximately $24.0 million from $17.3 million at the end of the first quarter Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities remained roughly flat from the first quarter at approximately $44.0 million SALT LAKE CITY – July 8, 2026 – Palladyne AI (NASDAQ: PDYN), a U.S.-based defense and industrial technology company delivering embodied AI-powered collaborative autonomy solutions, advanced avionics, precision-manufactured components, UAVs, and advanced aerospace engineering services, today announced preliminary financial results for its second fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2026. Select Preliminary 2Q26 Results In $M 2Q FY26 2Q FY25 2Q FY26 vs. 2Q FY 25 1Q FY26 2Q FY26 Vs. 1QFY 26 Revenue ~$5.8 $1.0 ~480% $3.5 ~66% Backlog ~$24.0 $1.7 ~1312% $17.3 ~39% Ben Wolff, President and Chief Executive Officer of Palladyne AI, commented: “The second quarter was another quarter where we delivered on our stated plan. Revenue grew substantially again, both year over year and sequentially vs Q1, and we continued to win new business across all of our operations. “Our plan for this year has been straightforward from the start. We had spent years building the underlying autonomy technology. With the acquisitions we completed in November, we became a vertically integrated, autonomy-based defense technology company, with the engineering, manufacturing and program capability that laid the groundwork for what we announced on June 8. “That announcement, our partnership with Israel Aerospace Industries , the largest Israeli defense company and pioneer of the loitering munition category more than 40 years ago, was a major step forward for us. This partnership gives us exclusive U.S. rights to a family of combat-proven systems, the HARPY, HAROP and Mini HARPY, that fill gaps in the U.S. arsenal for which there is no direct domestic equivalent. Despite hundreds of millions of dollars invested by others in this space, no other company has replicated what this family of loitering munitions systems delivers, particularly when it comes to battle-tested capabilities to suppress and destroy enemy air defenses. This partnership, together with the battlefield exercises we participated in this past quarter with SwarmOS™ and Gremlin-X™ and the first large purchase of our BRAIN flight computer by a defense prime for use on a counter-UAS system, has given us even greater optimism about the long-term prospects for our aerospace and defense business.” Second Quarter 2026 Preliminary Financial Highlights Revenue of approximately $5.8 million, an increase of approximately 480% compared to $1.0 million in the second quarter of 2025; Sequential revenue growth of approximately 66% compared to $3.5 million in the first quarter of 2026; Backlog of approximately $24.0 million as of June 30, 2026, up from $17.3 million as of March 31, 2026; Gross new contracts added during the quarter of approximately $12.5 million; Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $44.0 million as of June 30, 2026, roughly flat compared to March 31, 2026. Backlog and Contracted Demand As of June 30, 2026, backlog was approximately $24.0 million, up from $17.3 million as of March 31, 2026, reflecting approximately $12.5 million in new customer programs and contract awards secured across the Company’s operations during the quarter, net of revenue recognized. Backlog represents the total value of committed customer contracts and purchase orders. Palladyne AI expects a majority of this backlog to be recognized as revenue over the next 12 to 18 months. ### About Palladyne AI Palladyne AI is a U.S.-based technology company developing patented embodied artificial intelligence, collaborative autonomy solutions, advanced avionics, autonomous systems, advanced UAV engineering services, and precision-manufactured components for defense and industrial markets. Palladyne AI delivers secure, American-developed and operated platforms designed to meet the stringent requirements of U.S. government and public-sector customers, including data sovereignty, security, and compliance. Palladyne AI’s embodied AI is designed to operate in complex, contested, and high-risk environments, enabling distributed tasking, human-on-the-loop decision-making, degraded-communications resilience, and multi-domain coordination. Its platform-agnostic autonomy stack combines real-time sensor fusion, adaptive AI models, and edge-native orchestration, without vendor lock-in, to support autonomous and collaborative systems across air, ground, maritime, and industrial domains where performance, resilience, and trust are paramount. title: Notice Period Rules in India: Duration, Buy-Out, Recovery & Legal Rights 2026
summary: A comprehensive guide covering notice period laws, industry-wise duration, buyout calculation, garden leave, recovery rules, relieving letters, and employee & employer rights under Indian labour laws.
body_text: Insights & Resources Notice Period Rules in India: Duration, Buy-Out, Recovery & Legal Rights 2026 July 23, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet 1. What is a Notice Period? A notice period is the duration of time between an employee’s resignation (or termination by the employer) and their last working day in the organisation. It serves as a critical transition window that allows both parties to prepare for the separation in an orderly manner. During this period, the outgoing employee is expected to: • Complete pending tasks and ongoing projects • Hand over responsibilities, documents, and knowledge to a successor or team • Return company assets such as laptops, ID cards, access badges, and keys • Facilitate knowledge transfer sessions for continuity • Allow the employer adequate time to recruit or reassign a replacement For the employer, the notice period provides a buffer against sudden departures that could disrupt operations, damage client relationships, or cause loss of institutional knowledge. For the employee, it offers time to wrap up professional relationships and ensure a clean exit that protects their professional reputation and future career prospects. Key Point In India, notice periods are primarily governed by employment contracts and offer letters, not a single central law. The actual duration depends on your contract, company policy, seniority level, and the applicable state-level Shops & Establishments Act. 2. Legal Framework: Laws Governing Notice Period in India Unlike many Western countries where notice periods are standardised by national labour law, India does not have a single central statute that mandates a specific notice period for all private-sector employees. Instead, the legal framework is a patchwork of central laws, state regulations, and contractual provisions. 2.1 Industrial Relations Code, 2020 The Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020, which subsumes the Industrial Disputes Act 1947, applies primarily to “workers” and “workmen” in industrial establishments. Key provisions include: • Retrenchment Notice: Employers must give 1 month’s written notice (or pay in lieu) when retrenching workers in establishments with fewer than 300 employees. • For establishments with 100-299 workers: The notice period for retrenchment has been effectively increased to 60 days under the new provisions. • Establishments with 300+ workers: Prior government approval is mandatory before retrenchment, layoff, or closure. A simple notice is not sufficient. • Worker resignation: A worker must give 14 days’ notice before going on strike; for resignation, the contract or standing orders govern. 2.2 State Shops & Establishments Acts Each Indian state has its own Shops & Establishments Act that governs working conditions for commercial establishments, shops, restaurants, theatres, and other non-factory entities. Notice period provisions vary by state: • Maharashtra: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for termination after 3 months of service. • Karnataka: 30 days’ notice or pay in lieu for employees with more than 6 months of service. • Delhi: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for employees with more than 3 months of service. • Tamil Nadu: 30 days’ notice for termination of employees who have completed 6 months. • Gujarat: 30 days’ notice or salary in lieu for permanent employees. 2.3 Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020 The OSH Code applies to establishments with 10 or more workers and contract labour. While it primarily addresses workplace safety, it also contains provisions related to employment terms and conditions, including notice requirements for certain categories of workers. 2.4 Employment Contracts & Offer Letters For the vast majority of private-sector employees, especially in IT, BFSI, consulting, and other white-collar industries, the notice period is determined entirely by the employment contract or offer letter. These contractual notice periods are legally binding, provided they are reasonable and not unconscionable. Important Courts have generally upheld contractual notice periods of up to 90 days as reasonable. However, excessively long notice periods (such as 6 months) or unreasonable penalty clauses may be struck down as restraint of trade under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. 3. Notice Period Duration by Industry Notice period durations in India vary significantly across industries and seniority levels. The following table provides a comprehensive overview of standard notice periods across major sectors: Industry Junior / Entry Level Mid Level Senior / Leadership IT / Software 30 days 60 days 90 days BFSI (Banking, Finance) 30 days 60 days 90 days Manufacturing 30 days 30-60 days 60-90 days Startups 15-30 days 30 days 30-60 days Retail / Hospitality 15 days 30 days 30-60 days Pharma / Healthcare 30 days 60 days 90 days FMCG 30 days 30-60 days 60-90 days BPO / KPO 15-30 days 30 days 60 days Government / PSU 1-3 months 3 months 3 months India’s IT sector has among the highest notice periods globally . Major IT services companies such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCL Technologies typically require 90 days (3 months) of notice for confirmed employees. This is significantly longer than the 2-4 week standard in the United States or the 1-month standard in most European countries. The rationale for extended notice periods in IT includes the time needed for client relationship transition, project handover, knowledge documentation, and the critical nature of ongoing technology projects. Industry Insight Startups typically have the shortest notice periods (15-30 days) as they prioritise agility and speed. In contrast, Government and PSU roles often involve the longest notice periods (up to 3 months), reflecting bureaucratic processes and the time needed for formal transfers and charge handover. 4. Notice Period During Probation Probation periods are trial phases during which both the employer and the employee assess mutual fit. Notice period rules during probation are notably different from those applicable to confirmed employees. Standard Probation Notice Periods • Typical range: 7 to 30 days (as specified in the appointment letter) • Some companies allow termination with just 24 hours’ notice during probation • Probation notice is almost always shorter than the confirmed employee notice period • If not explicitly specified in the appointment letter, a reasonable notice of 15-30 days is generally expected by labour courts Key Considerations During probation, the employment relationship is more flexible. However, this does not mean either party can leave without any notice. Courts have held that even during probation, the principles of natural justice and fairness apply. • Always check your appointment letter for the specific probation notice clause • If the probation period is extended, the probation notice period typically continues to apply • Some companies require a different notice period once probation is confirmed mid-way • Exit during probation generally does not attract recovery or buyout penalties Pro Tip Before joining any organisation, carefully read the probation clause in your offer letter. Understand not just the duration of probation but also the notice period during probation, performance review criteria, and what happens if probation is extended. 5. Notice Period Buy-Out: Calculation & Process A notice period buy-out occurs when an employee (or their new employer) pays the current employer an amount equivalent to salary for the remaining unserved notice days, in order to leave before completing the full notice period. 5.1 When is Buy-Out Used? • Employee has received a better offer and the new employer needs them to join urgently • Personal or family reasons require an early departure • The employee is relocating to a different city or country • Critical project deadlines at the new employer require immediate joining • Mutual agreement between employee and current employer to end the relationship sooner 5.2 Buy-Out Calculation Formula Notice Period Buy-Out Formula Buy-Out Amount = (Monthly Salary / 30) x Unserved Notice Days Important: Some companies calculate the buy-out based on Basic Salary only, while others use Gross Salary (Basic + DA + HRA + other fixed components). Always refer to your employment contract for the exact clause. 5.3 Buy-Out Example Worked Example Employee: Rahul, Software Engineer at a Bengaluru IT firm Notice period: 90 days | Days served: 30 days | Unserved days: 60 days Monthly Gross Salary: Rs 80,000 Buy-Out = (Rs 80,000 / 30) x 60 = Rs 1,60,000 Rahul (or his new employer) must pay Rs 1,60,000 to the current employer for early release. 5.4 Who Pays the Buy-Out? Scenario Who Pays Notes Employee resigns & wants early release Employee Deducted from F&F or paid separately New employer reimburses New Employer Common in IT for senior hires Employer releases early (employer-initiated) Employer Must pay salary for full notice period Mutual agreement Negotiable Can agree on reduced amount or waiver 5.5 Tax Implications of Buy-Out • When employer pays notice salary in lieu of notice: Taxable as salary income for the employee under the Income Tax Act. • When employee pays buy-out to employer: This amount is NOT deductible as an expense under Income Tax for the employee. It is treated as a personal expense. • When new employer reimburses buy-out: The reimbursement is part of the new employment terms and is typically taxable as part of salary or a joining bonus. 6. Notice Period Recovery: What Employers Can Deduct When an employee leaves without serving the full notice period (and without a buy-out arrangement), the employer has the right to recover the notice period shortfall. This is known as notice period recovery. 6.1 Recovery Mechanism Employers have several mechanisms for recovering notice period dues: 1. Deduction from Full & Final (F&F) Settlement: The most common method. The employer deducts the unserved notice pay from the employee’s F&F amount, which includes pending salary, earned leave encashment, bonus, and other dues. 2. Withholding Relieving Letter: The employer can withhold the relieving letter and experience certificate until all dues (including notice recovery) are cleared. This is a powerful leverage point. 3. Civil Recovery: If the F&F settlement is insufficient to cover the recovery amount, the employer can pursue civil remedies under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 by filing a civil suit for breach of contract. 4. Background Verification Flag: Absence of a relieving letter is flagged by background verification agencies, which can impact the employee’s future job prospects. 6.2 Recovery Calculation Notice Period Recovery Formula Recovery = (Basic or Gross Salary as per contract / 30) x Unserved Days The exact salary component used for calculation (Basic Salary vs. Gross Salary) depends on the specific clause in your employment contract. In the absence of a specific clause, courts generally consider Basic Salary as the basis for recovery. Warning Absconding from a job without serving any notice period can have serious consequences. Beyond financial recovery, it can result in being blacklisted by the company (and sometimes the entire group), negative references during background checks, and difficulty obtaining a relieving letter. Always try to negotiate an early release rather than absconding. 7. Garden Leave: Meaning, Rules & Comparison Garden leave (also called “gardening leave”) is a period during which an employee who has resigned or been terminated remains on the company’s payroll but is not required to attend office or perform any work. The term originates from the British practice of “sending the employee home to tend their garden.” 7.1 Key Features of Garden Leave • The employee receives full salary and benefits during the garden leave period • The employee cannot join another employer or engage in competing business activities • Access to company systems, email, client lists, and confidential data is revoked • Commonly used for senior employees in competitive industries such as IT, BFSI, and management consulting • Duration is typically the full notice period or a significant part of it • The arrangement is legally enforceable as part of the employment contract 7.2 When Do Companies Use Garden Leave? • When a senior employee is joining a direct competitor • When the employee has access to highly sensitive client data or trade secrets • When there is a risk of the employee poaching colleagues or clients • When the company wants to ensure confidential strategic plans remain protected • When knowledge transfer is already complete, and physical presence adds no value 7.3 Garden Leave vs Notice Period vs Paid Leave Feature Notice Period (Working) Garden Leave Paid Leave Works for company? Yes No No Receives salary? Yes Yes Yes Can join competitor? No No (explicitly barred) N/A Company system access? Yes (full) No (revoked) No Knowledge transfer? Yes (primary purpose) No (already completed) N/A Purpose Smooth transition Competitive protection Rest & personal time Common for All employees Senior roles All employees Legal Note Garden leave clauses are generally enforceable in India because, unlike non-compete clauses (which are void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 post-employment), garden leave restricts activity during the employment period when the contract is still active and the employee is being compensated. 8. Early Release & Notice Period Waiver There are several scenarios where the full notice period may be shortened or waived entirely. Understanding these can help employees plan their transitions more effectively. Scenarios for Shortened Notice 1. Mutual Agreement: Both the employee and employer agree to a shorter notice period. This is the most common and smoothest route to early release. 2. Employee Buy-Out: The employee pays for the remaining unserved notice days. The employer is not obligated to accept a buy-out, but most companies have a buy-out provision in their policy. 3. Employer-Initiated Early Release: The employer decides to release the employee early. In this case, the employer must pay salary for the full contractual notice period. 4. Medical Emergency: Employees facing genuine medical emergencies (with supporting documentation from a registered medical practitioner) are often granted early release on humanitarian grounds. 5. No Critical Handover Needed: If the employee’s role does not involve critical projects or client relationships, and a replacement is already available, the employer may waive the remaining notice. 6. Replacement Already Hired: If the company has already found and onboarded a replacement, the remaining notice period may serve no practical purpose and can be waived. Negotiation Tip When requesting early release, frame it as a win-win. Offer to complete all handover documentation, train your replacement, and be available for questions via email or phone after your last day. Managers are more likely to grant early release when they feel confident that the transition will be smooth. 9. Legal Rights of Employees During Notice Period Employees in India have several important legal rights during their notice period. Understanding these rights ensures you are treated fairly and can make informed decisions. 1. Right to Resign: Every employee has the fundamental right to resign from employment. An employer cannot prevent an employee from resigning. The resignation takes effect once the notice period is served or bought out. 2. Right to Receive Full Salary: During the notice period, the employee is entitled to their full salary, allowances, and benefits as per their employment terms. The employer cannot reduce salary during notice. 3. Right to Use Earned Leave: Employees can utilise their accrued earned leave during the notice period, subject to company policy. Accrued earned leave is a statutory entitlement that cannot be forfeited. 4. Right to Receive a Relieving Letter: After serving the complete notice period and clearing all dues, the employee has the right to receive a relieving letter. Unreasonable withholding can be challenged in a Labour Court. 5. Right to Full & Final Settlement: The employee is entitled to receive their F&F settlement, including pending salary, leave encashment, bonus, and gratuity (if applicable), within 2 working days of their last working day under the new Labour Codes. 6. Right to Negotiate: Employees have the right to negotiate the notice period duration, request early release, or discuss buy-out terms. The employer is not obligated to agree, but negotiation is a legitimate right. 7. Right to Challenge Unfair Clauses: If the notice period clause in the employment contract is unconscionable or amounts to a restraint of trade, the employee can challenge it before a civil court or Labour Court. 10. Legal Rights of Employers Employers also have significant legal rights when it comes to notice periods. Understanding these rights helps employers protect their interests while ensuring compliance with labour laws. 1. Right to Enforce Contractual Notice: Employers can enforce the notice period as agreed in the employment contract. If the employee fails to serve notice, the employer can initiate recovery proceedings. 2. Right to Recover Notice Pay: If the employee leaves without serving the full notice, the employer can deduct the equivalent salary from the F&F settlement or pursue civil recovery. 3. Right to Withhold Relieving Letter: The employer can withhold the relieving letter and experience certificate until all outstanding dues, including notice period recovery, are cleared by the employee. 4. Right to Impose Garden Leave: Employers can place employees on garden leave during the notice period, restricting access to systems and clients while continuing to pay salary. 5. Right to Enforce Non-Compete During Notice: While post-employment non-compete clauses are generally void under Indian law, employers can enforce non-compete restrictions during the active notice period. 6. Right to Civil Remedies: For material breach of the employment contract (such as absconding or joining a competitor during notice), the employer can pursue civil remedies including injunctive relief and damages. 7. Right to Conduct Exit Process: Employers have the right to mandate exit interviews, asset return, knowledge transfer documentation, and security clearance as part of the notice period process. 11. Notice Period & Leaves: Can You Take Leave? One of the most frequently asked questions by employees serving notice is whether they can take leave during the notice period. The answer depends on company policy, the type of leave, and the terms of the employment contract. Types of Leave During Notice Leave Type Generally Allowed? Impact on Notice Period Earned Leave / Privilege Leave Yes (or encashed) Does not extend notice (most companies) Casual Leave Restricted by most companies May extend notice by equivalent days Sick Leave (with medical cert.) Yes (genuine illness) May extend notice by equivalent days Maternity / Paternity Leave Yes (statutory right) Runs concurrently or post-notice Compensatory Off At employer discretion Does not extend notice Leave Without Pay (LWP) Rare during notice Extends notice by equivalent days Key Rules • Most companies restrict casual leave and discourage sick leave during the notice period unless supported by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner. • Accrued earned leave is a statutory right. The employer cannot force forfeiture of earned leave; it can either be utilised (if the company allows) or encashed as part of the F&F settlement. • Some company policies state that any leave taken during notice extends the notice period by an equivalent number of days. Check your employee handbook or HR policy document for this clause. • Public holidays and weekly offs do NOT extend the notice period as they are not classified as leave. Best Practice If you plan to take leave during your notice period, communicate early with your manager and HR. Getting approval in writing (email confirmation) protects you from disputes about your last working day and F&F settlement date. 12. Relieving Letter: Importance & Rules The relieving letter is arguably the most important document issued at the end of an employment relationship. It serves as formal confirmation that the employee has been officially released from all duties and obligations. 12.1 What a Relieving Letter Contains • Full name of the employee • Employee ID or reference number • Designation and department at the time of exit • Date of joining and last working day • Confirmation that all company assets have been returned • Confirmation that all dues have been settled • Statement that the employee has been officially relieved from duties 12.2 Why is the Relieving Letter Critical? • Background Verification: Most reputable employers conduct background verification for new hires. The absence of a relieving letter from a previous employer is a major red flag that can lead to offer withdrawal. • Future Employment: Many employers require the relieving letter as a mandatory joining document. Without it, the new employer may not process your onboarding. • Legal Proof: The relieving letter serves as legal proof that you left your previous employment on good terms and fulfilled all contractual obligations. • Professional Reputation: A clean exit with a proper relieving letter reflects professionalism and protects your long-term career reputation. 12.3 What if the Employer Withholds the Relieving Letter? An employer cannot unreasonably withhold the relieving letter once the employee has served the notice period and cleared all dues. If the employer withholds without valid reason: • Step 1: Send a formal written request (email with acknowledgement) to HR and your reporting manager. • Step 2: Escalate to senior management with documented proof of notice served and dues cleared. • Step 3: Approach the Labour Commissioner or file a complaint with the local Labour Court. • Step 4: Courts can direct the employer to issue the relieving letter and may award compensation for the delay. 13. New Labour Codes 2026: What Changed The new Labour Codes, which consolidate 29 existing labour laws into 4 comprehensive codes, have introduced several changes that impact notice period rules and exit management in India. Key Changes Affecting Notice Periods Provision Old Rule New Rule (2026) Retrenchment Notice (100-299 workers) 30 days 60 days Establishments with 300+ workers Govt. permission for 100+ (some states) Govt. permission mandatory for 300+ (nationwide) F&F Settlement Timeline No statutory deadline Within 2 working days of last working day Fixed-Term Contracts Not clearly defined End of contract = end of obligation; no separate notice Standing Orders Applicable to 100+ workers Threshold may be revised based on state notification Impact on Employees • Faster F&F Settlements: The 2-working-day mandate for F&F settlement ensures employees receive their dues promptly upon exit. Previously, F&F could be delayed for weeks or even months. • Fixed-Term Clarity: Employees on fixed-term contracts now have clarity that the contract end date is the natural conclusion of the employment, and no separate notice period applies. • Greater Protection for Workers: The increased retrenchment notice period (60 days for establishments with 100-299 workers) provides a longer buffer for affected workers to find alternative employment. Impact on Employers • Compliance Burden: The 2-day F&F settlement timeline requires employers to have robust exit management and payroll systems in place. • Higher Retrenchment Threshold: The requirement of government approval for retrenchment in establishments with 300+ workers adds a procedural step that can delay workforce restructuring. • Documentation Requirements: Employers must maintain detailed records of notice periods served, buy-out payments, and F&F settlements to demonstrate compliance during audits. 14.
